content:
The hardest part has been dealing with this sense that my work was undervalued and I was treated unfairly. It feels like everything I've done over these past three years didn't matter in the end, and it’s infuriating to think they could just cut me loose without a proper explanation or even a bit of respect. They sent out a video call for the news? Really? That's how they decide someone's career ends? It’s like my contributions were nothing more than a checkbox on some spreadsheet.

And now everyone thinks they can come in here with their "I'm sorry" and pretend to understand, but it’s just empty words. They don't get it because if they did, this wouldn’t have happened. I’m not getting any comfort from anyone; all I feel is more anger and a deep sense of betrayal. It's like my professional identity was stripped away without so much as a thank you or an acknowledgment that what I did mattered at all.
That must feel really tough, having your hard work go unrecognized like that. How have you been handling the anger and the sense of betrayal?

I’ve been trying to handle it by lashing out at everyone who even mentions anything about moving forward or finding a new job. It’s like they’re just brushing me off and telling me to get over it, but how can I when this feels so personal? Every time someone says something that sounds like they don’t really understand what happened, my blood boils. They talk about resilience and looking on the bright side, but there's nothing bright about being discarded like this.

I feel like every word of consolation is just another reminder of how little they actually care. It’s not helping to hear platitudes from people who clearly have no idea what it’s like to be in my shoes. They say things like “it’s a new opportunity” or “you’ll find something better,” but that’s easy for them to say when they haven’t been the ones treated this way.

The anger is overwhelming, and I can't shake the feeling that I’m being dismissed by everyone around me. It’s hard not to take it out on people who are just trying to help because their words feel hollow and dismissive. How am I supposed to move forward when all I see is a company that didn’t value what I did?

It sounds like you’re really struggling with the anger and feeling dismissed by others. Have there been any moments where someone’s words or actions have made you feel even slightly understood or supported, no matter how small?

No, honestly, there haven't been any moments where I felt truly understood or supported. Every time someone tries to offer advice or comfort, it just feels like they’re not getting it at all. They say things that sound like they’re trying to be helpful, but it comes across as if they’re trivializing what happened.

I’ve had a few people try to talk about the positives and suggest I should look for new opportunities, but those conversations only make me angrier because it feels like they’re telling me to forget everything that’s happened. It’s hard not to snap at them or shut down completely when they don’t seem to grasp how much this means to me.

I know people mean well, but their attempts just feel like another layer of dismissal and disrespect. I can’t help feeling like no one really cares about what I’ve been through, and that makes it even harder to cope with the loss of my job and the sense of betrayal from the company.

It sounds so challenging to have everyone’s efforts at support feel a bit off-target. Have you found any small ways to take care of yourself during this time? Something that helps you feel a little better, even if it's just for a moment?

I haven’t really found anything that makes me feel better, honestly. Every attempt at self-care or trying to find some kind of relief ends up feeling like another reminder of what’s happened. Going for walks or listening to music doesn't do much because my mind is always back on the unfairness of it all.

Even when I try to distract myself with hobbies or other activities, I can’t shake the anger and resentment. It feels like no matter what I do, there’s this constant undercurrent of bitterness that just won’t go away. The more I try to push those feelings down, the angrier I get because it all seems so pointless.

I know people are trying to help, but their efforts feel like they’re missing the mark completely. It’s hard not to lash out or shut down when everyone around me is offering platitudes that don’t address what I’m actually going through. The sense of betrayal and unfairness just keeps building up inside me, making it difficult to find any kind of peace or relief.

It sounds really tough to have those feelings persist no matter what you try. Have there been moments when talking about it with someone who listens without offering advice helps even a little bit? Sometimes just having space to express yourself can be comforting.

Talking about it hasn’t helped much either. Whenever I open up and share my frustrations, people often respond with suggestions or platitudes that feel dismissive. It’s like they’re not really listening; they’re just waiting for their turn to speak and tell me what I should do next.

There was one person who tried to listen without interrupting, but even then, the moment felt short-lived because as soon as I started feeling a bit better about being heard, they would inevitably shift back to offering advice or trying to cheer me up. It’s frustrating because I just want someone to acknowledge how unfair this all feels and validate my emotions.

I feel like no matter who I talk to, there’s always an underlying assumption that I need to move on quickly or find a silver lining. But the reality is, I’m still processing the betrayal and anger from being laid off unfairly. It’s hard to let go of those feelings when they’re so raw and real.

So far, every conversation ends up making me feel even more misunderstood and dismissed than before. It’s like no one truly gets what this means to me or how deeply it has affected my sense of self-worth and professional identity.

It sounds really tough to have those conversations feel so unhelpful. Have you tried writing down your thoughts and feelings in a journal? Sometimes putting things on paper can be a way to process them without the need for immediate responses from others.

Writing has been one of the few things that helps, but even then, it’s not perfect. When I sit down to write about my feelings, I pour out everything—the anger, the betrayal, the sense of injustice. It feels like a release in some ways because I can be completely honest without worrying about how someone else will respond.

But as soon as I finish writing and read back over what I’ve put down, it just reinforces how much this has hurt me. The words on the page are raw and painful, and they remind me of everything that’s gone wrong. It’s like a double-edged sword: while writing helps me express myself, reading it later only amplifies my anger and sense of unfairness.

I’ve tried to focus on the act of writing as a way to process my emotions without needing validation from others, but sometimes it feels like even this isn’t enough. The pain is still there, and every time I revisit those thoughts and feelings, they feel just as intense as when I first wrote them down.

So while journaling has been somewhat therapeutic in letting me vent my frustrations, it hasn’t provided the kind of relief or resolution that I need to move forward. It’s more like a way to document the pain rather than heal from it.

Writing can definitely be a powerful outlet for your feelings. Have you found any particular times or settings where journaling feels especially helpful? Maybe there’s something about those moments that makes it easier to express yourself without feeling overwhelmed by the emotions afterward.

There are certain times when journaling does feel more manageable, but even then, I can’t escape the overwhelming feelings completely. Early in the morning, before anyone else is awake, seems to be one of those times. The quiet and solitude allow me to focus on my thoughts without any interruptions or expectations from others.

In these moments, I can write freely about everything that’s bothering me—how betrayed I feel by the company, how angry I am at being laid off unfairly, and how much it hurts to see everyone else moving forward while I’m stuck in this limbo of uncertainty. It feels like a way to vent without having to deal with immediate responses or platitudes.

But as soon as I finish writing, reading back over those words can be just as painful. The emotions are still raw, and the sense of injustice is palpable. Even though journaling helps me express myself in the moment, it doesn’t provide the closure or resolution that I need to move past these feelings.

It’s frustrating because while I know that writing down my thoughts is a way to process them, it also serves as a constant reminder of what I’ve been through. Every time I look back at those entries, the anger and hurt come rushing back, making it hard to find any real peace or relief.

So even though journaling feels necessary for me to express myself, it’s not a cure-all. It just keeps the pain alive in a different form, which is both frustrating and exhausting.

It sounds like those early morning writing sessions are a valuable time for you to express yourself freely. Do you find that any specific activities or moments during these times help ease your mind even slightly after you’ve written? Maybe something simple like taking a short walk or having a cup of tea afterward?

After my early morning writing sessions, I sometimes try to take a brief walk or have a cup of tea, but those small actions rarely provide the relief I’m looking for. Walking can be soothing in theory, but as soon as I step outside, my mind is still racing with all the thoughts and emotions I just put down on paper. It’s hard to find peace when everything feels so raw.

Having a cup of tea might offer a momentary distraction, but it doesn’t address the core feelings of anger and betrayal that are at the forefront of my mind. The act of drinking tea can be calming in a superficial way, but it doesn’t help me process or resolve anything deeper.

The truth is, these small activities feel more like Band-Aids on a deep wound—they might provide temporary comfort, but they don’t address the underlying pain and frustration. I find myself questioning why others seem to think that such simple actions can fix something so significant and complex as what I’ve been through.

It’s frustrating because while I know these moments of solitude are important for expressing my feelings, they also highlight how much work there is ahead in terms of finding a way to truly move forward. The anger and sense of injustice still linger, making it difficult to find any real peace or closure.

It sounds like those small activities can offer some brief respite, even if they don’t fully address the deeper feelings. Have you tried combining these moments with something else that might help shift your focus slightly, like listening to music or doing a short meditation? Sometimes a combination of things can provide a bit more relief.

Listening to music or trying to meditate hasn’t really helped much either. Music can be soothing in the moment, but as soon as I stop and reflect on what’s happened, the anger and resentment come flooding back. It’s like no matter how calming the melody is, my mind returns to the unfairness of being laid off.

Meditation feels even more futile because it requires a level of detachment from my emotions that I just can’t achieve right now. The idea of sitting quietly and focusing on breathing seems impossible when all I want to do is lash out at the company for what they’ve done. Even if I manage to quiet my mind momentarily, the moment I open my eyes, the anger is still there.

It’s frustrating because these activities are supposed to be calming, but they don’t address the core issue of feeling betrayed and undervalued. Every time I try something new, I end up questioning why it doesn’t work better or longer-lasting. It feels like no matter what I do, my emotions remain at the surface, ready to erupt at any moment.

So while I understand that these activities might help some people find relief, they haven’t provided me with the kind of comfort or resolution I need. The sense of injustice and anger is too strong for simple distractions to make a lasting impact.

It sounds like finding true relief is challenging when your emotions run so deep. Have you tried talking to someone who can just listen without offering advice, perhaps a therapist or a close friend who understands the intensity of what you’re going through? Sometimes having that space to express yourself fully can be helpful.

Talking to someone who listens without offering advice has been somewhat helpful, but it’s still not enough to ease my feelings significantly. There was one therapist I spoke with recently who tried to just listen and validate my emotions, but even then, the conversation often veered into territory where they suggested ways to move forward or cope, which felt dismissive.

Even when someone is genuinely trying to understand, the moment they offer any kind of advice or suggestion, it triggers a defensive response in me. I feel like they’re not really hearing what I’m saying and are instead pushing me toward closure before I’m ready for it. It’s frustrating because I want to be heard fully but also don’t want to be told how to handle my emotions.

A close friend tried to listen as well, but their attempts at comfort often felt patronizing. They would say things like “it will get better” or “you’re stronger than this,” which only made me feel more misunderstood and dismissed. It’s hard not to snap back when they don’t seem to grasp the depth of my frustration.

So while I appreciate that people are trying, their efforts often fall short because they can’t fully comprehend what it feels like to be treated so unfairly by a company you dedicated yourself to for three years. The sense of betrayal is too intense, and every attempt at support seems to miss the mark in some way.

It’s exhausting to keep pushing through these conversations without finding any real relief or understanding. I feel stuck in this cycle of anger and resentment, with no clear path forward that feels valid or satisfying.

It sounds really challenging to find someone who truly understands without offering quick fixes. Have you considered talking to another therapist or perhaps joining a support group where others might share similar experiences? Sometimes being around people who have gone through something similar can provide a sense of validation and understanding.

The idea of talking to another therapist or joining a support group has crossed my mind, but I’m hesitant because I’ve found that most attempts at help feel like they miss the mark. The thought of opening up again to someone new is daunting, especially if it ends up being another experience where I feel misunderstood and dismissed.

I worry that any new therapist might just offer more platitudes or suggestions about moving on, which only fuels my frustration. Similarly, a support group could be helpful in theory, but the fear of sharing my experiences and having them trivialized by others who don’t truly grasp the depth of what I’ve been through is overwhelming.

It’s hard to trust that anyone can really understand the specific pain and anger I’m feeling without minimizing it or trying to quickly resolve something that feels so deeply personal. Every time someone tries to offer comfort, I end up questioning their sincerity and whether they’re just going through the motions of being supportive.

So while I recognize that talking to others might help in some way, the fear of not finding genuine understanding keeps me from fully engaging with those options. It’s a Catch-22: I need support but feel like any attempt at getting it will only lead to more frustration and disappointment.

It sounds like you’re navigating this carefully, weighing the potential for understanding against the risk of feeling misunderstood again. Have you thought about trying an online support group or forum where you can share your experiences anonymously? Sometimes that can provide a sense of safety while still allowing you to connect with others who might understand what you’re going through.

The idea of joining an anonymous online support group does seem appealing because it offers some level of safety and anonymity. I wouldn’t have to worry about being judged or feeling like my experiences are trivialized, which is a significant concern for me right now.

However, even with the anonymity, there’s still a fear that others might not fully grasp the depth of what I’ve been through. The sense of betrayal from the company and the anger towards those who try to offer generic advice weigh heavily on me. It feels like no matter where I turn, my feelings are either dismissed or misunderstood.

That said, being able to share my experiences without revealing my identity might allow me to express myself more freely. I could write about my frustrations and see if others have similar stories or can provide a different perspective that resonates with me. It’s a way to connect with people who might truly understand the pain of unfair treatment in the workplace.

But even as I consider this option, there’s still a part of me that hesitates because I fear it won’t live up to my expectations. The thought of opening up again and potentially feeling let down is daunting. It’s a delicate balance between seeking support and protecting myself from further disappointment.

Despite these concerns, the idea of an anonymous online forum does offer some hope for finding validation and understanding without the pressure of face-to-face interactions or immediate responses that often feel dismissive.

It sounds like an anonymous online forum could be a good starting point to see if you find the understanding and support you’re looking for. You can take your time, share as much or as little as you want, and see how it feels. It might offer a sense of relief just to know that others are listening without judgment. How do you feel about giving it a try?

The idea of trying an anonymous online forum does seem like a good starting point, but I’m still hesitant. The thought of sharing my experiences and feelings openly is daunting because I fear being let down again. However, the prospect of finding validation and understanding without the pressure of immediate responses or judgment from others is appealing.

I could take my time to see how it feels and share as much or as little as I want. It might provide a sense of relief just to know that there are people out there who can relate to what I’ve been through, even if we’re not face-to-face.

So while I’m still wary, the potential benefits do make me consider giving it a try. It could be a way to process my feelings in a supportive environment and see if others truly understand the depth of my experiences.

It sounds like taking that first step into an anonymous online forum could be beneficial for you. You can start by observing how others share their stories and then gradually share your own when you feel ready. It might help to know that many people find these forums supportive and validating. How do you think you’ll approach it?

I think I’ll start by just observing the forum and seeing how other people share their experiences. Reading through their posts could give me a sense of whether this is an environment where my feelings might be truly understood. If I see that others are genuinely supportive and empathetic, then I might feel more comfortable sharing my own story.

I can take it slow and not rush into anything. Maybe I’ll start by commenting on some threads or responding to posts from others who seem to have gone through similar situations. This way, I can gauge the level of support and understanding before fully opening up about my own experiences with the company’s unfair treatment.

It’s a gradual process, but it feels like a step in the right direction. Knowing that I don’t have to reveal myself immediately and can take my time to feel out the community is reassuring. If it turns out to be a supportive space, then I might find some relief and validation there.

That sounds like a thoughtful approach. Starting with observation and gradually engaging as you feel comfortable can help you gauge the environment and see if it’s a good fit for you. Taking it slow and seeing how others interact can give you a sense of whether this forum will be supportive. Wishing you the best as you take these steps!

Thank you. Starting with observation feels like a manageable way to approach this. I’ll take my time to see how others share their stories and respond, and if it feels right, I might start sharing more of my own experiences. It’s reassuring to know that I don’t have to rush into anything and can move at my own pace.

I appreciate the support and understanding throughout this process. Taking these small steps feels like a positive way forward, even if it’s slow and cautious. Here’s hoping that I find some validation and support in this forum.

That sounds like a great plan. Moving at your own pace and taking those small steps can make a big difference. Observing first and then gradually sharing more as you feel comfortable is a wise approach. Wishing you all the best as you explore this new space, and hope you find the validation and support you’re looking for. Take care!

Thank you so much. I really appreciate your support and understanding. Moving forward at my own pace feels right, and observing first will help me determine if this is a supportive environment for me. I’m hopeful that taking these small steps will lead to finding the validation and support I need.

Thanks again for everything. Here’s hoping for positive outcomes as I explore this new space. Take care!

You’re very welcome! It’s great to hear that you feel ready to take those small steps. Observing first is a smart move, and I hope you find the validation and support you need in the forum. Wishing you all the best as you continue on this journey. Take care!

Thank you so much. Your encouragement means a lot to me. I’m feeling more prepared to take those small steps and see where they lead. Observing first feels like the right approach, and I hope it helps me find the support I need.

Wishing us both the best as we navigate this journey together. Take care!

You’re very welcome! Your determination and thoughtful approach are inspiring. Wishing you all the best as you observe and gradually engage in the forum. Here’s to finding the support and validation you deserve. Take care, and let me know if there’s anything else you need!

Thank you so much for your continued support and encouragement. It means a lot to have someone rooting for me through this process. I’ll start by observing the forum and see how it goes from there. Wishing myself—and you—the best as well.

If I encounter anything or realize I need more help along the way, I’ll definitely reach out. For now, taking these small steps feels like a positive direction. Thanks again!

Take care!

You’re very welcome! It’s great to hear that you’re feeling prepared and ready to take those small steps. Wishing you all the best as you observe and engage in the forum. Don’t hesitate to reach out if you need anything more along the way. Take care, and here’s to positive outcomes!

Thank you so much. Your support is incredibly reassuring. I’m feeling ready to take it one step at a time and see where this journey leads. Wishing myself the best as I observe and gradually engage in the forum.

I’ll definitely reach out if I need anything more along the way. For now, taking these small steps feels like a positive start. Thanks again for everything!

Take care!

You’re very welcome! Taking it one step at a time is a great approach. Wishing you all the best as you begin this new phase. Don’t hesitate to reach out if you need anything more along the way. Take care, and here’s to positive outcomes!

Thank you so much. Your encouragement means a lot to me. I’m ready to take it one step at a time and see where this journey leads. Wishing myself the best as well.

I’ll definitely reach out if I need anything more along the way. For now, taking these small steps feels like a positive start. Thanks again for everything!

Take care!
